Emily (Design): Quick design ping — exploring an inline accordion for invoices where each line item can expand to show a small token histogram and quick actions (download, dispute). Sketch: https://figma.com/... :eyeglasses: Sanjay (PM): Love the compactness. Main ask: can users still scan totals at-a-glance? worried expansion will hide context. :thinking: Marta (Frontend): Curious about perf — rendering histograms for 50 rows could be heavy. Maybe lazy-render on expand? Tyler (Eng): Agreed on lazy-render. Also we should cap to svg sparklines rather than canvas to keep bundle small. Emily (Design): Proposal: collapsed state shows amount + tiny sparkline svg (20x40). expand reveals histogram, token breakdown, copy for invoice line, and CTA buttons. Olivia (Product): Two product decisions: 1) default scope toggle (Org vs Project) should control whether these accordions aggregate or show per-project lines. 2) persistent download CTA for the whole invoice should stay top-right. Sanjay (PM): +1. Also suggest an affordance for switching token denomination (tokens vs USD) inline. Use a small toggle inside the header of the accordion. Marta (Frontend): Implementation note: header toggle could be a11y trap if focus order not managed. Might want to open keyboard nav flow: "tab into accordion header" -> "arrow keys" to move between accordions -> "enter/space" to expand. Tyler (Eng): For keyboard nav we can reuse the existing list pattern from /usage; it'll minimize JS. Also prefer aria attributes on the button controlling the panel. Example snippet: ```html
``` Marta (Frontend): For the small histogram we can inline a simple SVG path with viewBox and stroke; that keeps DOM light. For the expanded token histogram maybe render as lightweight bars using CSS grid. a11y-bot: Accessibility note: ensure aria-expanded state updates on toggle; provide visible focus ring, and announce the change with screen reader-friendly text, e.g., "Expanded line item for , showing token usage". Also color contrast for histogram bars must meet 3:1 for non-critical info and 4.5:1 for important labels. Emily (Design): Copy question: inside expanded panel, what label should we use for token breakdown? "Token usage (in thousands)" vs "Estimated token count"? Which is clearer? Olivia (Product): "Token usage" is fine but include units. For billing docs customers often want both tokens and USD estimate. Show tokens primary, USD small caption. Sanjay (PM): UX nit: when many rows are expanded, we should sticky the invoice header (totals) so you don't lose context. Might also collapse others automatically if user expands a new one (optional setting). Tyler (Eng): Auto-collapse other rows could be simple state logic but annoys power users. Preference: keep it optional behind a user-level setting. Marta (Frontend): Performance fallback: if invoice has >100 lines, switch to paginated or condensed mode without histograms. We can surface a banner: "Large invoice detected — switching to condensed view" with an opt-in button to load full detail. Emily (Design): Accessibility-cognizant microcopy for condensed mode: "Showing condensed invoice for performance — show full details" (button). a11y-bot: Also ensure the condensed banner is keyboard focusable and announced by SR when it appears. Olivia (Product): One more: analytics — track expand events, token-toggle changes, download clicks. We need that to evaluate whether histograms help customers. Sanjay (PM): Agree. Event names: invoice.line.expand, invoice.line.toggle_units, invoice.download. Keep payload small: invoice_id, line_id, scope (org|project). Marta (Frontend): Dev question: any preferred threshold for auto-lazy-render? e.g., only render histograms after user has hovered or focused for 300ms? Tyler (Eng): Hover-based render could be weird on keyboard. Better: render on expand or on focus-in if collapsed. Use IntersectionObserver for lazy offscreen rows when user scrolls. Emily (Design): OK next steps: I'll update the Figma with two variants — "single-expand" and "multi-expand with sticky header" and add copy suggestions. Olivia (Product): Thanks — please also add a11y notes in the spec. I'll review for product intent after design update. Sanjay (PM): Schedule a short alignment with eng + frontend tomorrow 11am PT? Marta (Frontend): I can make a prototype of the small sparkline + expand animation before then. Tyler (Eng): I'll draft the aria pattern and a minimal implementation plan. Emily (Design): Awesome. Tagging @a11y-bot for follow-up checklist when I post the updated spec. :heavy_check_mark:
